to hold

the same as ἔχω [to have]. The present form was invented by grammarians (such as Arcadius p. 155, 17. 156, 14): Homer and other poets used only the aorist ἔσχεθον σχέθοιμι σχέθω σχεθεῖν σχεθών [I held, may I hold, I hold, to hold, holding], as in the examples collected in Thes. vol. 7 p. 1651. The infinitive and participle in manuscripts are almost constantly written with the wrong accent σχέθειν [to hold] and σχέθων [holding].
In the sense of holding.

The same pattern of compounds: ἐπισχεθεῖν [to hold upon] (Sept. 453 κεραυνού δέ νιν βέλος ἐπισχέθοι [may the thunderbolt's missile hold him back], which passage I should have mentioned under ἐπέχω) and κατασχεθεῖν [to hold down] (κατασχεθών [holding down] Suppl. 1067.).
